Lingayats.fact: The Lingayats (IPA: [liŋɡaːjɐt̪ɐ]) are a monotheistic religious denomination of Hinduism. Lingayats are known for their unique practice of Ishtalinga worship, where adherents carry a personal linga symbolizing a constant, intimate relationship with Parashiva.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: Lingayatism is generally considered a _____ sect because their beliefs include many Hindu elements
Lingayats.fact: Unlike mainstream Hinduism, Lingayats reject scriptural authority of vedas, puranas, superstition, astrology, vedic priesthood ritualistic practices, and the concept of rebirth, promoting a direct, personal experience of the divine. Lingayatism is generally considered a Hindu sect because their beliefs include many Hindu elements.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: Worship is centered on Shiva as the universal god in the iconographic form of _____
Lingayats.fact: Worship is centered on Shiva as the universal god in the iconographic form of Ishtalinga.

Lingayats.fact: In historical literature, they are sometimes called Lingawants, Lingangis, Lingadharis, Sivabhaktas, Virasaivas or Veerashaivas.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: The istalinga is an oval-shaped emblem symbolising _____, the absolute reality and icon of their spirituality
Lingayats.fact: The istalinga is an oval-shaped emblem symbolising Parashiva, the absolute reality and icon of their spirituality.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: The terms _____ and Veerashaiva have been used synonymously

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: The present-day dispute involves two opposing groups, one seeking separate status for the _____ community and the other wanting to keep the Veerashaiva-Lingayat community united
Lingayats.fact: Veerashaivism refers to the broader Veerashaiva philosophy and theology as well as the movement, states Blake Michael, while Lingayata refers to the modern community, sect or caste that adheres to this philosophy. Lingayats.fact: Basava grew up in a Brahmin family with a tradition of Shaivism. Lingayats.fact: Basavanna spread social awareness through his poetry, popularly called Vachanaas. Basavanna rejected gender or social discrimination, and caste distinctions, as well as some extant practices such as the wearing of sacred thread, and replaced this with the ritual of wearing Ishtalinga necklace, with an image of the Shiva Liṅga, by every person regardless of his or her birth, to be a constant reminder of one's bhakti (loving devotion) to god Shiva.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society

Lingayats.fact: In 1167 the Veerashaivas were repressed, and most of them left Kalyāna, Bijjala's new capital, spreading Basava's teachings into a wider area in southern India.

Lingayats.fact: Basava's nephew Channabasava organised the community and systematised Virasaiva theology, moving the Virashaiva community toward the mainstream Hindu culture.

Lingayats.fact: In 2000, the Akhila Bharatha (All India) Veerashaiva Mahasabha started a campaign for recognition of "Veerashaivas or Lingayats" as a non-Hindu religion, and a separate listing in the Census.

Lingayats.fact: According to Gauri Lankesh, Veerashaivism is preserved and transmitted by five peethas (Rambhapuri, Ujjaini, Kedar, Shreeshail, Kashi), which play an essential role in the Veerashaiva tradition.

Lingayats.question: It is viewed as a "living, moving" divinity of the _____ devotee
Lingayats.fact: The Lingayats always wear the ishtalinga held with a necklace. It is viewed as a "living, moving" divinity of the Lingayat devotee.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: Thus bhakti progresses from external icon-aided loving devotional worship of _____ to deeper fusion of awareness with abstract Shiva, ultimately to advaita (oneness) of one's soul and god for moksha
Lingayats.fact: Thus bhakti progresses from external icon-aided loving devotional worship of Shiva to deeper fusion of awareness with abstract Shiva, ultimately to advaita (oneness) of one's soul and god for moksha.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society

Lingayats.fact: In particular, the Shunya Sampadane texts present the ideas of Allama Prabhu in a form of dialogue, where shunya is that void and distinctions which a spiritual journey seeks to fill and eliminate.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: It is the described as state of union of one's soul with the infinite _____, the state of blissful moksha
Lingayats.fact: According to Schrader, Lingayats believe that if they live an ethical life then this will be their last life, and they will merge into Shiva, a belief that has fed the confusion that they do not believe in rebirth. It is the described as state of union of one's soul with the infinite Shiva, the state of blissful moksha.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: This Lingayat concept is similar to shunya Brahma concept found in certain texts of _____, particularly in Odiya, such as the poetic Panchasakhas
Lingayats.fact: This Lingayat concept is similar to shunya Brahma concept found in certain texts of Vaishnavism, particularly in Odiya, such as the poetic Panchasakhas. However, both in Lingayats and various flavors of Vaishnavism such as Mahima Dharma, the idea of Shunya is closer to the Hindu concept of metaphysical Brahman, rather than to the Śūnyatā concept of Buddhism.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: Bhrityāchāra – _____ towards all creatures
Lingayats.fact: Bhrityāchāra – Compassion towards all creatures.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: Ganāchāra – _____ of the community and its tenets
Lingayats.fact: Ganāchāra – Defence of the community and its tenets.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society

Lingayats.fact: It means "work is heaven" or "to work [Kayakave] is to be in the Lord's Kingdom [Kailasa]".

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: The slogan is attributed to _____, and generally interpreted to signify a work ethic for all social classes
Lingayats.fact: The slogan is attributed to Basava, and generally interpreted to signify a work ethic for all social classes.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: Lingayat poet-saints accepted the concept of karma and repeatedly mention it in their _____ poetry
Lingayats.fact: Lingayat poet-saints accepted the concept of karma and repeatedly mention it in their Shiva poetry. For example, states Ramanujan, Mahadeviyakka mentions karma and resulting chain of rebirths that are cut short by bhakti to Shiva.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: For example, states _____, Mahadeviyakka mentions karma and resulting chain of rebirths that are cut short by bhakti to Shiva
Lingayats.fact: For example, states Ramanujan, Mahadeviyakka mentions karma and resulting chain of rebirths that are cut short by bhakti to Shiva.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: These ideas, states _____, are similar to those found in Bhagavad Gita which teaches "work must be done without any attachment to the results"
Lingayats.fact: According to Schouten, Siddharama and Allama debated the doctrine of karma as the law of work and merit, but Allama persuaded Siddharama that such merit is a low-level mechanism, and real mystical achievement transcends "the sphere of works and rewards" and is void of self-interest. These ideas, states Schouten, are similar to those found in Bhagavad Gita which teaches "work must be done without any attachment to the results".

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: According to _____, skilful work and service to one's community, without discrimination, is a means to experiencing the divine, a sentiment that continues to be revered in present-day Virasaivas
Lingayats.fact: According to Virasaivism, skilful work and service to one's community, without discrimination, is a means to experiencing the divine, a sentiment that continues to be revered in present-day Virasaivas.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society

Lingayats.fact: According to Jan Peter Schouten, this doctrine is philosophically rooted in the more ancient So'ham Sanskrit oneness mantra related to Shiva, and which means "I am He".

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: Upon attaining the age of 8–11 years, the child receives _____ from the family Guru to know the proper procedure to perform pooja of ishtalinga
Lingayats.fact: Upon attaining the age of 8–11 years, the child receives Diksha from the family Guru to know the proper procedure to perform pooja of ishtalinga.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society

Lingayats.fact: In addition, they have continued to build the community halls and Shaiva temple traditions of South India.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: However, the prayers and offerings are not led by _____ priests but by Lingayat priests (Veerashaiva Jangama)
Lingayats.fact: However, the prayers and offerings are not led by Brahmin priests but by Lingayat priests (Veerashaiva Jangama).

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: The temple format is simpler than those of Jains and Hindus found in north _____
Lingayats.fact: The temple format is simpler than those of Jains and Hindus found in north Karnataka. Lingayats.fact: In particular, these include various Vachana (literally, "what is said") such as the Shat-sthala-vachana, Kala-jnana-vachana, Mantra-gopya, Ghatachakra-vachana and Raja-yoga-vachana.

Lingayats.fact: Saints and Sharanas like Allamaprabhu, Akka Mahadevi, Siddarama and Basava were at the forefront of this development during the 12th century.

Lingayats.subject: Indian Society
Lingayats.question: It rejected various forms of ritualism and the uncritical adherence to any text including the _____
Lingayats.fact: The 13th-century Telugu Virashaiva poet Palkuriki Somanatha, author of Basava Purana—a scripture of Veerashaivas, for example asserted, "Virashaivism fully conformed to the Vedas and the shastras."
